title: Fuzzy correlation evidence bundler for PagerDuty cards
creator: Aisha Coleman
description: Build a service that assembles compact, correlated evidence bundles from traces, metrics, and logs and attaches them to PagerDuty incident cards and Slack incident threads. The goal is to reduce time-to-triage by providing a single view with prioritized signals (top anomalous metrics, heaviest traces, representative log excerpts) and lightweight links to expanded artifacts. The bundler should use fuzzy heuristics to correlate telemetry across sources when exact request IDs are missing, surface uncertainty scores, and provide operator quick-actions (open dashboard, trigger rollback, link to runbook).
acceptance_criteria: Bundles include: top 3 anomalous metrics (with short description and Grafana link), one or two representative traces (span list + trace link), and up to 10 log excerpts prioritized by error-level and time proximity.
PagerDuty incident cards receive a condensed JSON attachment (<= 40KB) and a user-visible preview with summary + high-confidence action buttons (view dashboard, run runbook, open trace).
Slack incident thread posts a human-readable summary with a link to full bundle in our evidence service and one-click actions for oncall (ack, trigger rollback script, add postmortem draft).
Correlation uses at least two fuzzy matching signals (time-window alignment, IP/session fingerprint, top-N span similarity) and surface an uncertainty score in the UI.
End-to-end test covering: synthetic incident generator -> metrics anomaly detection -> trace selection -> log sampling -> bundle assembly -> PD card attachment -> Slack thread post.
Performance: bundle assembly latency <= 1s for common cases (<=200ms for cached prefix), 95th percentile attachment delivery to PD/Slack <= 3s.
Security: no customer PII is included in attachments; KMS encryption is used for persisted bundles and audit logging records attachment events.
notes: Design trade-offs: full fidelity attachments are heavy (many MBs). We choose compact summaries + links to full artifacts stored in S3 behind signed URLs. This reduces PD/Slack quota usage and keeps attachments within payload limits.

Heuristics: initial fuzzy correlator will weigh time proximity (40%), span-name similarity (30%), shared top-level tags like client_ip or user_agent fingerprint (30%). We'll iterate weights based on false-positive rate from pilot.
Privacy: redact user identifiers by default. Add a per-customer allowlist flag for richer bundles (enterprise customers only, toggle controlled in Tenant config).

Failure modes: if evidence service is unavailable, PD card should still attach a lightweight placeholder and Slack should show a queued indicator. We will implement exponential backoff + buffer and SLA for bundler fallback.

Rollout plan: start with a small pilot (internal infra teams) -> expand to non-prod customers -> opt-in beta for production tenants -> global rollout after metrics meet signal-noise and latency targets.
updates: 2026-03-02: Spike completed to evaluate matching signals. Found that relying solely on time windows produced too many false matches for high-throughput services.
2026-03-04: Prototype service up (trace fetcher + Prometheus anomaly puller). Initial bundle shape defined (summary + links).
2026-03-06: Security review kickoff: discussed PII redaction and signed URL expiry defaults (1h for internal, 15m for external).
2026-03-08: Integration spec reviewed with PM and Design (notes in Confluence). PM requested uncertainty score visualization and an operator-facing confidence tooltip.

2026-03-10: Implemented first fuzzy correlator using time-window + top-3 span-name Jaccard similarity + client IP fingerprint. Running locally against replay data with synthetic incidents. False positive rate ~12% on replay set.

2026-03-12: GitHub PR opened for evidence-service (redaction + bundling) and PD adapter. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/1427. Seeking review from @sanjay and @leah for security and PD adapter edge cases.
